title: Much Ado About Nothing — 30th Summer Season
excerpt: Thank you for June 10–28, 2026 at Pinkney Park. The 30th summer season of Much Ado About Nothing has ended.
content:
Shakespeare on the Sound celebrates 30 seasons of storytelling under the stars with Much Ado About Nothing, directed by David Frederick Mold.

Shakespeare's sparkling comedy transports audiences to 19th-century Sicily, where romance blooms, tempers flare, and a battle of wits becomes a battle of hearts. Enjoy a brilliant ensemble in one of Connecticut's most beloved outdoor settings.

Performances ran June 10–28, 2026 (no shows Mondays) at 7:30pm, Wednesdays through Sundays, at Pinkney Park, Rowayton, CT.

VIP reserved seating pre-sale was April 7–14. General admission opened April 15. Adults $25, children 12 and under $5. Pay-What-You-Will performances were Tuesday, June 16 and 23. Those tickets are no longer on sale.

title: Thank You: Much Ado About Something Gala
excerpt: The October 16, 2026 gala at The House Up on the Hill has ended. Tickets are no longer on sale.
content:
Thank you for Much Ado About Something on Friday, October 16, 2026, 6–10pm at The House Up on the Hill, 26 Seir Hill Rd., Norwalk, CT.

The evening of cocktails, bites, dancing, and auctions is over, and tickets are no longer on sale. Gifts to Shakespeare on the Sound are welcome anytime.

title: 2026 Season Sponsors Announced
excerpt: We thank DR Bank, Neil Hauck Architects, R+C, Russo & Rizio, Rowayton Seafood, and Fairfield County Bank for supporting our 30th season.
content:
Shakespeare on the Sound's 2026 summer production is made possible by generous community partners: DR Bank, Neil Hauck Architects, R+C, Russo & Rizio, Rowayton Seafood, and Fairfield County Bank.

Their support helps keep professional Shakespeare accessible under the stars at Pinkney Park and funds our year-round education programs across Fairfield County.

title: 2026 Tickets Have Closed
excerpt: Much Ado About Nothing ticket sales have ended. Thank you for June 10–28 at Pinkney Park.
content:
Tickets for the 2026 season have closed. Thank you for Much Ado About Nothing, June 10–28 at Pinkney Park.

General admission was $25 for adults and $5 for children 12 and under. VIP reserved seating was $75. Student and senior rush seating was $15 at the park box office on the day of the show.

Pay-What-You-Will performances were Tuesday, June 16 and 23. The Apprentice Company matinee was Saturday, June 20. Those evenings are over, and nothing from that calendar is on sale.

title: Shakespeare for Kids in the Park
excerpt: Accessible Kids' Show at 6:30pm every evening — a 30-minute Much Ado adaptation by our Apprentice Company, plus tours for schools and libraries.
content:
A 30-minute version of Much Ado About Nothing for ages 1–100! A kid-friendly adaptation by our Apprentice Company that also serves as a refresher for those who need a plot reminder.

6:30pm in the park, every night before the MainStage show. Kids' Shows are accessible to all — show up, find a spot, and enjoy!

Education is at the cornerstone of Shakespeare on the Sound. We provide workshops, touring shows, and summer camps across Fairfield County. To book at your library or school, use our education inquiry form on the Learning page.

title: Celebrating 30 Seasons in Rowayton
excerpt: Since 1996, Shakespeare on the Sound has brought professional outdoor Shakespeare to Pinkney Park — starting with Much Ado About Nothing.
content:
In 1996, Rowayton's 6th Taxing District gave permission for the first production in Pinkney Park. The inaugural show was Much Ado About Nothing — an estimated 6,000 audience members attended.

Thirty seasons later, we return to that beloved comedy under the stars, continuing our mission to produce affordable, professional open-air Shakespeare for Fairfield County.

Learn more about our history on the About page.
